Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

where adverb

in what place?

also where?, where are you?, in which place

classical

Plaut. Rud. 238: Dīc ubi es?
Ter. Hec. 84: ubi tē oblectāstī tam diū?

ubi

adverb, interrogative and relative, of rest in a place

where? where

Only of being somewhere: “where to?” is quō, “where from?” unde. As a relative it answers ibi, there. Ubi is also the conjunction “when”, a different record.

Other words

  • ubi gentium (ubi terrārum) — where on earth?

    ubi with a partitive genitive · also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 469: ubi tū es gentium?

Examples

  • Dīc ubi es? … ubi es? — Ecce mē. accēde ad mē atque adī contrā.

    Tell me where you are? … Where are you? — Here I am. Come to me, come this way.Plaut. Rud. 238–242

  • Dīc mihi, Philōtis, ubi tē oblectāstī tam diū?

    Tell me, Philotis, where have you been enjoying yourself all this time?Ter. Hec. 84

  • dīc nōbīs ubi sīs futūrus, ēde audācter, committe, crēde lūcī

    tell us where you will be; out with it boldly, trust it to the daylightCatull. 55.15–16

  • mīrātus dīcēs: “hoc, rogō, crēvit ubi?”

    you will say in wonder: “Where, I ask you, did this grow?”Mart. 13.58.2

  • hoc erat in vōtīs: modus agrī nōn ita magnus, hortus ubi et tēctō vīcīnus jūgis aquae fōns et paulum silvae super hīs foret

    this was what I prayed for: a piece of land not so very big, where there would be a garden, and near the house a spring of ever-flowing water, and a bit of woodland besidesHor. S. 2.6.1–3

See also where to, where from, where is …?, there, here.
